Now a more productive comment: 
1. The experience of a couple who applied for a visa 5 years ago or even 3 years ago is completely irrelevant to the present. It sounds like you were heavily misled by random people instead of following credible resources. I strongly advise you to understand that in order to succeed in this process on your own you must follow complicated bureaucracy which cannot be done if you don't follow credible resources.

2. I completely didn't understand the comment about the lawyer entering the office. Entering to do what? A lawyer can't open a partner visa application for you by walking anywhere, the application is done strictly online, including by lawyers.

3. The lawyer is correct you can't enter Israel before you've been properly invited. Once you applied you're an immigration applicant and not a tourist.

4. You must apply where you actually live. Your partner must update his address to where he actually lives and only then apply. You will lose precious time if you try to cut corners with the city of residence thing.
